chief_complaint: shoulder and hip stiffness with high ESR
hpi_details: A 54-year-old female presents to the clinic with shoulder and hip stiffness and a high ESR. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she developed frozen shoulders and hip arthritis from lifting heavy gardening soil and sleeping in a drafty bedroom.
concerns: She is worried that she is rapidly losing her independence because she can barely lift her arms to comb her hair or get out of bed without help.
expectations: She hopes to get a cortisone injection or fast-acting medication that will loosen up her stiff joints so she can move freely.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Polymyalgia Rheumatica is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

After excluding important mimics and screening urgently for giant cell arteritis, PMR is typically managed with clinician-directed glucocorticoids and a monitored taper individualized to response and adverse-effect risk.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: shoulder and hip stiffness in elderly patient, high ESR

Key HPI features: A 54-year-old female presents to the clinic with shoulder and hip stiffness in an older adult, with a high ESR. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Rheumatoid arthritis (elderly onset) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Missing giant cell arteritis: new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, or any visual symptom requires same-day emergency assessment to protect vision.
management_principles: Arrange prompt clinician-directed glucocorticoid treatment only after assessment for giant cell arteritis and relevant mimics; do not use response to steroids as the sole diagnostic test
Monitor glucocorticoid toxicity and preventive care, including blood pressure, glucose, infection risk, bone protection, and tapering under the treating clinician's direction
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
reference_soap.plan: Screen immediately for giant cell arteritis and arrange emergency assessment for visual symptoms. Use clinician-directed glucocorticoid treatment and taper with monitoring for adverse effects. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Polymyalgia Rheumatica
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Polymyalgia Rheumatica

teaching.one_liner: An inflammatory condition in adults aged 50 years or older causing symmetric shoulder and hip girdle stiffness and aching, often with elevated inflammatory markers.
red_flags: New headache, scalp tenderness, or jaw pain when chewing (possible giant cell arteritis)
Any visual change, double vision, or transient vision loss: seek emergency care immediately
Fever, marked weight loss, or focal weakness suggesting infection, malignancy, or an alternative diagnosis

must_ask.say: Is the stiffness in both shoulders and hips equally?
How long does the morning stiffness last?
Any new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, double vision, or vision loss?
How long have you had this?

history.answer: My shoulders and hips feel so stiff and sore, and it has been getting harder to move around over the past few weeks.
It affects both sides equally, right deep in both shoulders and both of my hips.
It started about three weeks ago out of nowhere and has been gradually getting worse.
It is a deep, aching tightness that reaches about a five or six out of ten at its worst.
No, I have not seen any swelling, redness, or heat in my shoulders, hips, or knees.
Yes, mornings are definitely the hardest; I wake up completely stiff, and it takes an hour or two to loosen up.
Sitting still makes the stiffness settle right back in, but gentle walking around during the day helps ease it a bit.
It has been very hard to raise my arms to brush my hair, put on my coat, or get up from a low sofa.
No, I haven't had any high fever, sweating, or chills.
No, I haven't fallen, twisted any joints, or heard any popping sounds.
No, I have never had any joint stiffness or pain like this before.
I have been feeling unusually tired and worn out recently, though my weight has stayed about the same.
No, I haven't had any skin rashes, mouth sores, hair loss, or dry eyes.
No, I do not have severe morning back stiffness, heel pain, or sausage-like swelling in my fingers or toes.
No, I haven't had any sore throat, stomach flu, diarrhea, or burning when I urinate.
No, I haven't been drinking heavily or eating large amounts of seafood, and I don't take water pills.
No, I have never taken steroid pills, had joint injections, or undergone joint surgery.
I have been in a monogamous marriage with my husband for thirty years and have no new sexual partners.
No, I haven't had any new or throbbing headaches, and my scalp does not feel sore when I comb my hair.
No, my jaw does not ache, cramp, or get tired when I chew food.
No, my vision is completely normal, with no blurring, double vision, or temporary loss of sight.
I thought maybe I gave myself frozen shoulders and bad hip stiffness from overdoing yard work and sleeping near an open window.
I'm terrified that I'm losing my independence because some mornings I can't even raise my arms to brush my hair or get dressed.
I'm hoping you can give me a shot or some medicine to loosen up these joints so I can dress myself without agonizing pain.
I have always been healthy and don't have any chronic conditions like hypertension, diabetes, or rheumatoid arthritis.
I have never had any operations or stayed overnight in a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or health supplements.
No, I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked in my life.
I only have a glass of wine on rare social occasions, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an administrative assistant at an elementary school and live with my husband.
No one in my immediate family has had autoimmune disorders, rheumatoid arthritis, or lupus.
My periods stopped about three years ago when I went through menopause, so pregnancy is not possible.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Well-nourished and comfortable at rest, but moves stiffly and grimaces slightly when adjusting posture or attempting to lift her arms.
Visual acuity intact bilaterally, pupils equal and reactive to light, extraocular movements full, and normal funduscopic exam without optic disc edema or pallor.
Temporal arteries are soft, non-tender, non-thickened, and normally pulsatile bilaterally with equal radial and carotid pulses.

Active abduction and flexion of both shoulders and flexion of both hips are restricted by stiffness and pain, while passive range of motion is nearly full with mild end-range discomfort and no joint swelling, warmth, or erythema.
Normal muscle bulk and tone throughout, with full five out of five strength in all four extremities when pain inhibition is accounted for.
No cutaneous rashes, facial erythema, psoriatic plaques, subcutaneous nodules, or tophi.
Cervical and thoracolumbar spine demonstrate preserved alignment without midline spinous process tenderness or paraspinal muscle spasm.
Gait is steady and non-ataxic, but noticeably cautious and stiff around the hips.
